articles.summary: Segundo o Washington Post, verba havia sido aprovada para países afetados pela guerra na Ucrânia e para o Oriente Médio. Dinheiro irá a governos latinos alinhados à Casa Branca.
articles.body:
O governo do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , está redirecionando para países da América Latina recursos que haviam sido aprovados para ajudar aliados na Europa e no Oriente Médio. As informações foram reveladas pelo jornal The Washington Post nesta quinta-feira (1º).

Segundo o jornal, os recursos somam "dezenas de milhões de dólares" em assistência militar e haviam sido autorizados pelo Congresso para outros países.

No mês passado, o Departamento de Estado informou ao Congresso que pretendia redirecionar parte das verbas para a América Latina. De acordo com o Washington Post, a decisão levou dois parlamentares democratas a suspenderem a liberação dos recursos.

Na quarta-feira (30), porém, o governo Trump informou ao Congresso que não respeitaria a suspensão e seguiria com o repasse. O jornal obteve a informação com três fontes com conhecimento do assunto.

Ao todo, a Casa Branca pretende destinar US$ 52 milhões (R$ 271 milhões) a Panamá, Peru, Equador e Colômbia. Segundo o Washington Post, os recursos estavam previstos originalmente para Eslováquia, Macedônia do Norte, Tunísia e Iraque.

Ao jornal, o Departamento de Estado afirmou que o dinheiro será melhor utilizado na América Latina. Segundo o governo, a decisão vai ao encontro da política de Trump de priorizar a influência dos EUA no continente americano.

O Departamento de Estado afirmou ainda que os recursos serão usados para fortalecer "parcerias de segurança dos EUA" e neutralizar a "influência militar adversária" na região.

Peru, Equador e Colômbia passaram recentemente por mudanças de governo, com a eleição de candidatos de direita. Os três países se aproximaram dos Estados Unidos e anunciaram medidas de combate ao narcotráfico na região, uma das prioridades de Trump.

Em relação ao Panamá, a relação com os Estados Unidos chegou a ficar estremecida no ano passado, depois que Trump ameaçou tomar o controle do Canal do Panamá. No início deste ano, o governo panamenho afirmou que a crise havia sido superada.

articles.title: Special prosecutor taking over investigation of Cornell University gang rape allegations as new details emerge
articles.summary: Snapchat messages exchanged during the alleged assault at Cornell University include a photo of then-student Jane Doe in a room at the fraternity house, acco...
articles.body:
New York State Attorney General Letitia James will be taking over as special prosecutor in the case alleging sexual assault at Cornell University, Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Thursday, saying she "lost faith" in the district attorney's ability to oversee it.

The announcement comes as new details have emerged this week about the alleged gang rape of then-student Jane Doe in a room at the Chi Phi fraternity house in 2024, including what she told campus police about the alleged assault.

"New information has raised serious questions about how this case was handled, and I've lost faith in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee it," Hochul said in a statement. "The young woman at the center of this case deserves to know that every fact will be examined and justice pursued."

James will now have the power to investigate the incident and, if warranted, prosecute any offenses and present evidence to a grand jury. Cornell told CNN Thursday it supports the governor's decision.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten has repeatedly told CNN that his office never received more than the Snapchat messages and a six-page investigative report before deciding not to bring charges in the case.

In the report, Doe she recounted being hit and feeling emotionally coerced into sexual activity while intoxicated.

She made a more explicit accusation of rape in a November 2024 interview with campus police – the transcript of which Van Houten told CNN his office never received .

Cornell has said police followed protocol and shared "all investigatory information" with the DA. But many questions remain about the initial investigation and what the county district attorney knew about the allegations. Here's what we know:

Snapchat messages exchanged during the alleged assault in a group chat titled "Chi Phi Actives" include a photo of then-student Jane Doe in a room at the fraternity house, according to images of the chain obtained by CNN.

The conversations taking place on the fast-erasing messaging app suggest other photos or videos might have been recovered had there been a more thorough criminal investigation, according to a source close to the case.

CNN has previously reported messages in the group chat that stated "free p*ssy" upstairs and asked, "Shop still open?"

Additional images of messages obtained by CNN include a reference to one member "laying rn," and other members asking, "are you guys at least naked?" and stating, "Like you can walk in and whip it out rn."

In the three weeks between when the former student was allegedly gang raped to her describing the night to campus police, Doe appeared to wrestle with shame and her stance had evolved on whether an assault took place, according to records obtained exclusively by the New York Times and corroborated by Doe's attorney.

In an article published Thursday, the Times cited documents from the university's formal Title IX investigation that shed new light on how Doe initially viewed the night's events, discussed them with her roommates and communicated with some of the men before she reported her allegations to university police.

"Ms. Doe's internal processing went from denial, to shame and ultimately acceptance that she had been raped by people that she thought were her friends," her attorney, Thomas P. Giuffra, told CNN Thursday. "Her reactions were a textbook reaction to trauma."

CNN has not seen the Title IX filings, which are generally confidential and restricted to the parties involved.

Cornell's investigation yielded hundreds of pages of emails, text messages, photos and interviews with Doe, her friends and six of the seven men she accused, according to the Times. The files also included an extensive transcript of the original police interviews with Doe, the Times reported.

After the alleged gang rape at Chi Phi fraternity that began on October 19, 2024, Doe recounted the night's events to her roommates without identifying herself as a rape victim, the Times reported, citing the files.

The following narrative comes from the Times' review of the Title IX files it obtained:

Doe reportedly told her two roommates the day she returned home that she had consumed ketamine and had sex with multiple men. One roommate told investigators that Jane Doe did not use the word "rape" or "assault" yet.

One roommate said she could not remember Doe saying yes to anything that occurred while another roommate said it appeared Doe was "in shock," the roommate told investigators, "not really understanding the gravity of what she was saying."

The next day, Doe reportedly spoke with her sorority big sister, who later told investigators "what she was going through is that she had not yet processed what had happened."

Doe had also communicated with at least two of the men she later accused of sexual assault, according to the Times.

One reportedly sent Doe a text message which said: "I just wanted to apologize for how things went down the other night." The sender said he and another male who was allegedly involved felt terrible and too under the influence of drugs and alcohol to "shut it down and kick people out before it got way out of hand."

Doe replied to the man reassuringly, the Times reported, saying "non of the sexual stuff was illegal."

But once she came to terms with what happened, she went to a health professional a few days after the incident, Doe's attorney told CNN.

A heavily redacted, 99-page document obtained by CNN summarizes key evidence included in a Cornell disciplinary panel's decision.

"I felt like bait. I felt like lions around me. It was just a totally debilitating place to be in," Doe told Cornell investigators in a hearing months after her alleged assault at the Chi Phi fraternity, according to the panel's findings.

While CNN has been unable to view the entire document due to redactions, it describes the heavy presence of ketamine at the fraternity house on the night of the alleged assault, as well as Doe's reported state of mind at certain points.

Doe described the effects of ketamine as "vague consciousness," according to the panel's decision.

"You look like an operating human being… You don't look dead or asleep necessarily. So, lights are on, but nobody's home. Your brain is not functioning at its proper level," she said.

Details previously reported by CNN describe Doe telling police she consumed ketamine on the night of the assault.

The panel's decision also cites a recorded phone call Doe had with one of the defendants in early November 2024, where they discussed ketamine and other substances they took as the initial sexual activity began on the night of the alleged assault.

Doe started recording her phone calls after the alleged assault so she could have a "reference to the limited information she was receiving," as she sought to process what happened, according to Giuffra.

Doe also recalled being "naked" in a fraternity house bed at some point during the night of the alleged assault while two men stood by, according to the decision. "They felt more like voyeurs than anything," she said in a November interview with investigators.

A few days after the incident, Doe went to Cornell Health to get treated for a urinary tract infection and to get tested for sexually transmitted diseases, her attorney said.

"Ms. Doe disclosed to the treating health care professional that she contracted the UTI in a 'traumatic way,'" Giuffra said about the October 22 visit.

"Ms. Doe's disclosure warranted further inquiry, including a rape kit, consultation of medical professionals trained to deal with rape cases and a physical exam to document her injuries," her attorney said. "Inexplicably, all the medical professional did was to advise Ms. Doe to 'speak with somebody.'"

CNN asked the university for comment on Giuffra's claims against Cornell Health. "At this time, we have no new information" beyond Cornell's previous statements about the case, a Cornell spokesperson said Thursday.

Giuffra said Cornell Health failed to act during a critical window for obtaining evidence.

"Timing is vital for rape kits because DNA evidence is lost over time," the attorney said. "Critically, two days after the assault, a rape kit would likely have revealed DNA which would have been significant information for a criminal investigation. However this was not offered or suggested."

Doe's attorney said he doesn't know whether the trove of details from the Title IX investigation was ever given to Cornell police.

"I believe that the information was not, because what is contained in the proceedings is evidence of several crimes being committed with excellent supporting evidence," Giuffra said in a statement to CNN.

Giuffra said his office did not give the documents to the Times – but he's grateful someone did.

"There are strict privacy policies in Title IX proceedings and access to these documents are limited to school officials, involved parties and their lawyers," Giuffra said in his statement. "I want it to be clear that we were not responsible for leaking these documents."

But "frankly, I am glad it was leaked," he said. "It just shows how badly this whole tragedy was handled from all sides. Even medical providers did not do the right thing."

Report details how Doe came to understand the night as assault

In the weeks after the alleged gang rape, interviews with Doe, her roommates and her sorority big sister describe a 20-year-old sophomore realizing the severity of the night's events and understanding them as an alleged assault, according to the Times.

The documents reportedly detail how rumors about the alleged gang rape led her to fear reputational damage and left her humiliated.

It was an evolution of thought complicated by Doe's history as a sexual assault survivor, the Times reports, citing the documents. In the six-page summary signed by Doe to police, she described having a prior "traumatic experience" regarding sexual intercourse.

After the alleged rape, Doe saw comments on an online forum about Greek life about Chi Phi brothers drugging and gang raping a sophomore, which she later told investigators: "That's the first time I had ever heard the narrative change that I wasn't a whore and that I was assaulted," the Times reported.

On November 3, Doe texted one of the men, explicitly saying that what happened on that October night was not consensual. According to the Times, she wrote: "let's be clear that 90% of what happened that night was not consensual. i was given more key than i can remember," using a shorthand for ketamine, "and i know that i told u i felt uncomfortable and i didn't know anyone in the room."

Before going to campus police, Doe reportedly collected evidence, including photos of the bruises on her body allegedly caused by one of the men hitting her. She also had not washed the dress to save as potential evidence, the Times reports.

On November 7, Doe went to an emergency room in Ithaca, where Cornell is located, and requested a rape kit, the Times reported, citing the documents.

In a 2024 statement to Cornell police, obtained by CNN from a source familiar with the investigation, Doe recounted arriving at the Chi Phi fraternity house and dancing with one person who asked if she would be interested in participating in a threesome . Doe told police she was "pretty ok" with aspects of an initial encounter, but that later in the night she did not consent to other sexual activities, according to the six-page statement.

"I felt like I was unable to make any decisions because of how intoxicated I was," she said in the statement. Doe said she felt like her overall intoxication level at one point was about an "8 out of 10" — which she said was the most intoxicated she had been in her life.

She described being "pretty incapacitated," feeling uncomfortable, swatting one man's hand away several times and being "horrified" as more men entered the room they were in. She said she "finally gave in" to one later encounter after she was asked "to have sex so many times," according to the statement.

"To me that felt like coercion," she said in the statement. "Also, I felt like due to my intoxication, they should have known how intoxicated I was based on how I was slurring my words."

'I can say with 100% confidence I was raped'

Doe made a more explicit accusation of rape in a separate document, according to CNN affiliate WCBS . The station obtained a transcript of a November 2024 interview with campus police from a source.

"I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," Doe said in the transcript, according to WCBS.

CNN has not seen the transcript and has asked Cornell for a copy but has not heard back. The transcript is a separate document from the six-page statement that was submitted by the university.

Beyond alleged emotional pressure, Doe told police in the statement she was physically hit and remembered feeling hurt. "One hit in particular sent a sharp pain through me," she said. The student also described noticing bruising on her body the following day.

Doe also said she "had become extremely uncomfortable with how this night was turning out" and thought, "if I passed out and the men had sex with me, then they could be charged with Rape," the statement reads.

Doe told police she remembered consuming a "heavy amount" of ketamine, smoking marijuana and having "various things" poured on her body. She said she initially agreed to having drugs consumed off her body while feeling "extremely tired" but "couldn't tell what they were pouring on me."

Doe reported the alleged incident to Cornell police on November 8, 2024, weeks after the alleged assault, according to a civil complaint filed last month. In the days following the alleged incident, she was "traumatized, numb and unable to function or accept the horror of what had happened," her attorney told CNN.

Frat member advised Doe to avoid Halloween party, source says

Cornell's internal investigation revealed Doe planned to return to the fraternity house the following week for a Halloween party, according to two sources familiar with the school's Title IX investigation.

But a fraternity official spoke with Doe before the party and advised her not to go, one of the sources told CNN. The source said fraternity members, Doe's friends and Doe herself mentioned this in their testimonies during Cornell's investigation.

"It was all part of her processing what had happened. She was still in the denial stage," her attorney said. "She could not accept what happened to her."

In the following days, Doe reported the October incident to Cornell police, according to her lawsuit.

DA's office says it never received the transcript

Van Houten told CNN his office was not given the interview transcript before deciding no charges should be filed in the investigation.

The DA told CNN on Wednesday morning that the university had still not provided his office with the transcript. CNN had also reached out to Van Houten about whether it received the Title IX filings.

The DA said it was Doe's six-page statement that determined no charges should be filed, adding, "Multiple prosecutors and criminal investigators reviewed Jane Doe's statement and correctly determined the alleged facts as set forth in the statement do not constitute a crime."

Van Houten said he learned of the more explicit allegation made in the interview when he was contacted by WCBS on Tuesday evening and said his office will be investigating the reported statements "fully."

When reached by CNN about the DA's comments, a Cornell University spokesperson did not specifically address the transcript but said it "shared all investigatory information" with the DA's office.

The university likely did not break any laws if it did neglect to share all relevant documents with the DA, said former prosecutor Gary Galperin. But he said not sharing all documents would violate "all principles of what's logical and decent."

The DA's comments Wednesday raised new questions about what law enforcement knew in the weeks after the alleged assault and why no criminal charges were filed.

"It is a case that, clearly, just on the face of her statement, is so complex and so nuanced," former Westchester County District Attorney Mimi Rocah said

"If you're an investigator trying to get at the truth, as this DA office should have been, they should have sought more information," she added.

Van Houten canceled his scheduled appearance on CNN Wednesday evening, saying, "At this time I need to shift my focus to the investigation and to pursuing the additional evidence that has recently come to light."

He said his office will keep the public informed of developments in the investigation and any action of the Tompkins County Grand Jury.

After Doe's allegations, "Cornell established the Presidential Task Force on Campus Sexual Assault, comprising faculty, staff, and students, in early 2025," the university said .

"Our goal is not simply to respond appropriately when sexual misconduct is reported, but to build a community in which sexual violence is prevented, people feel safe coming forward, those who do are supported, and individuals found responsible are held accountable."

But some Cornell students who were on campus in 2024 said the university's response hasn't been enough.

"The main problem I see in the university's response … is the lack of ownership," said Hayden Watkins, executive vice president of the Cornell Student Assembly.

He also said the school's task force on campus sexual assault is not representative.

"There's been very little student voice throughout this entire process," Watkins said. "That task force included roughly 20 individuals, but only two people were undergraduate students."

The unfolding details of Jane Doe's case have sparked renewed attention to the ongoing topic of sexual assault awareness and prevention on college campuses.

Doe's attorney has said Cornell expelled two of the seven accused students while the others received lesser punishments, including suspensions, workshops or written assignments.

Cornell has countered that claim, saying "none of the individuals charged were offered the opportunity to write essays as a sole consequence of their involvement."

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Cornell has agreed to an outside investigation to "determine whether Cornell met every obligation to protect its students and pursue justice," she told CNN. The university confirmed that it agreed to the investigation and declined to provide further details.

The Chi Phi national fraternity said Wednesday that it condemns sexual assault and drug and alcohol abuse, and three days after Doe filed a police report, the fraternity chapter "voted unanimously to remove the accused members from its rolls" and "recommended that our national fraternity permanently expel them," which it said the fraternity's Grand Council did in a subsequent meeting.

"These actions went beyond anything the law or Cornell University required of us," the fraternity added in the statement.

The school also said it had closed that chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity in 2024, and that the chapter remains barred from campus.

It is unclear if any of the accused men are still Cornell students.

Help is available : For help in the US, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 or chat 24/7 on online.rainn.org .

articles.title: Michael Keaton's 1992 Batmobile, built on a chassis from two Chevrolet Impalas, is heading to auction with an estimate of up to $7 million
articles.summary: The 1992 Batmobile associated with Michael Keaton’s Batman is heading for auction this November, with Julien’s Auctions estimating that the screen-used
articles.body: The 1992 Batmobile associated with Michael Keaton’s Batman is heading for auction this November, with Julien’s Auctions estimating that the screen-used vehicle could sell for between $5 million and $7 million. Built for Tim Burton’s Batman Returns, the car was constructed around a chassis made from two Chevrolet Impalas, then transformed into the long, low-slung machine seen on screen. Its upcoming sale puts one of the most recognisable film cars of the 1990s back in the spotlight, more than three decades after it appeared alongside Keaton’s version of the character. The auction will also include other Batman costumes, props and production material from the franchise’s film and television history.How two Chevrolet Impalas became Michael Keaton’s BatmobileThe car began with something considerably more ordinary than its finished appearance suggested. Its chassis was formed by combining parts from two Chevrolet Impalas, providing the underlying structure for the vehicle that would eventually become Burton’s Batmobile.As reported by Julien's Auctions, Carl Casper, the automotive designer and builder behind the project, was responsible for turning that foundation into the distinctive machine required for Batman Returns. Much of the exterior was shaped by hand, while the front end was designed around a jet-turbine-inspired nose. The result was deliberately unlike a conventional production car, with its long body and enclosed cockpit helping establish the visual identity of Burton’s Gotham.The vehicle was not simply a prop placed in the background. It was built to serve as Batman’s principal mode of transport within the film, making it one of the production's most recognisable physical objects.Michael Keaton’s car returns to the auction marketKeaton drove this version of the Batmobile in Batman Returns, which reached cinemas in 1992. The second film retained the darker visual language of its predecessor while introducing a different collection of characters and settings around Bruce Wayne.For viewers who associate Keaton’s Batman with the Burton films, the car is closely tied to that period of the franchise. Its shape became part of the character’s screen identity rather than simply an accessory to the costume. Julien’s Auctions and Turner Classic Movies have now announced The Ultimate Batmobile Auction, with the Hero Batmobile from Batman Returns as its main attraction. Reportedly, the sale is scheduled for November 23, 2026, with bidding taking place both live and online.The Batman Returns Batmobile is estimated at up to $7 millionJulien’s has placed an estimated value of $5 million to $7 million on the Batman Returns Batmobile. That earlier record involved the original car created for the 1966 television series starring Adam West. George Barris’ Batmobile sold for $4.6 million in 2013, making it the reference point for major Batmobile sales for more than a decade. The new estimate therefore places Keaton’s screen-used car in a different financial bracket. Whether it reaches the upper end of the range will depend on bidding when the auction takes place.How the Batmobile shaped Michael Keaton’s Batman eraThe Batmobile is inseparable from the look created for Burton’s two Batman films. The 1989 movie had already moved the character away from the brighter visual style associated with the 1960s television series, and Batman Returns continued that approach. The car fitted into that setting. Its bodywork was unusually elongated, its cabin was enclosed, and the front section suggested a futuristic machine rather than a modified road car. The hand-built construction allowed the production team to create something that could exist within the stylised version of Gotham presented on screen.Michael Uslan, one of the figures behind the Batman film franchise, has also highlighted the Batmobile as part of the character’s essential screen mythology. Batman may have no superpowers, but his equipment and vehicles have long been central to how the character is represented in film.Batman’s 60-year screen history comes together at Julien’s auctionThe November sale is being presented as a wider collection of Batman-related material rather than a single-vehicle auction. Julien’s says costumes, props and other production artefacts from Batman’s film and television history will also be offered.More lots are expected to be announced before the sale. That gives the event a broader connection to the character’s screen history, spanning different versions of Batman rather than concentrating exclusively on Burton’s films. The original Batman television series starring Adam West turns 60 in 2026, linking the upcoming auction with a much earlier period in the character’s live-action history.Michael Keaton’s Batmobile could surpass the 1966 car’s $4.6 million recordThe contrast between the two major Batmobiles is striking in practical terms. Barris’ 1966 car represented the colourful television era of Batman, while Casper’s machine belonged to Burton’s much darker interpretation more than two decades later. Their auction histories now provide a useful marker of how valuable major Batman production vehicles have become to collectors. The 1966 Batmobile reached $4.6 million in 2013. The 1992 version has been given an estimate that extends to $7 million. For the Batman Returns car, the next chapter will be written on November 23. Until then, the vehicle remains a piece of film-production history that began with two Chevrolet Impalas and ended up becoming Michael Keaton’s Batmobile.You use AI every day. articles.title: Why is Barapullah Phase III choking Delhi traffic: Sharp merges, bottlenecks and design flaws
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Twelve years after work began and barely two days after Barapullah Phase III corridor opened, Delhi is back at the drawing board.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Twelve years after work began and barely two days after Barapullah Phase III corridor opened, Delhi is back at the drawing board.The traffic chaos on the new stretch has prompted Delhi Traffic Police to examine not just the freshly inaugurated section but the design of the entire Barapullah corridor.A drone survey and joint meeting with PWD have now put the corridor’s lane configuration, merging points and traffic flow under the scanner.The problem became clear on Wednesday morning. Thousands of motorists followed the new route, expecting the promised 15-minute journey between Mayur Vihar and INA. Instead, many found themselves crawling for two hours or more.The congestion continued Thursday, with some motorists who had used the route a day earlier choosing to stay away, while those who tried it again found themselves in another jam. The frustration soon moved online.Barapullah fix? Barricades or cones to create tapered, smoother mergeA commuter posted, “The flyover is a total mess. Five-km traffic jam today also. Traffic stuck for hours. God forbid, for emergency someone cannot even take a detour anywhere. This is a PUBLIC HAZARD. Needs to be closed ASAP.”Traffic police’s first finding was the new road was not the whole problem. Some of the trouble was waiting further down. The new corridor has three lanes, but these eventually fe­ed into the two-lane existing Barapullah stretch. That sudden reduction becomes particularly problematic when traffic volumes surge.The exercise has helped officials identify specific points where the flow can be imp­r­o­ved without waiting for another major construction project.The survey found a significant mismatch in lane capacity at key merging points, with multiple streams of traffic co­nverging towards the existing Barapullah flyover, which has comparatively less capacity.At key points, more traffic is being funnelled into a road with less capacity. The most significant bottleneck identified so far is near Sarai Kale Khan close to the loop around Sundial Park, where traffic coming from the loop joins the new Barapullah elevated stretch. Instead of traffic gradually blending into the main carriageway, the two streams meet abruptly because of the sharp geometry of the merge.Officials said this creates a bottleneck, particularly when traffic volumes are high. Their immediate solution is decidedly less glamorous than the Rs 1,000-crore-plus infrastruct­u­re around it: better channelisation using barricades or cones to create a tapered, smoother merge.Another problem spot has been identified in the older section, where traffic from the Guru Harkrishan Medical Institute side merges with Barapullah. Traffic personnel have been asked to remain deployed at crucial times to regulate vehicles and facilitate stop-and-go movement.Officials are also examining whether traffic can be regulated or diverted towards NH-24 wherever feasible, reducing the pressure on the Barapullah corridor.Then came the digital traffic cop.Google Maps had already decided that Barapullah was the route to take. The newly opened corridor appeared smooth on the app, making it a seemingly shorter and faster option and directing motorists towards it. Traffic police have raised the issue with Google, sources said.According to the sources, Google responded that its real-time traffic system needs a few days of actual traffic data after a new road opens before it can accurately reflect conditions. So, while the road was still learning how to handle Delhi’s traffic, the app was already sending Delhi’s traffic onto it.For now, traffic police and PWD are looking at physical channelisation, manual regulation, possible diversion towards NH-24 and corrections to navigation-app routing.The irony is hard to miss: a 12-year-old project was opened to make commute smoother, and within 48 hours, officials were studying where the road itself needs help.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Putin warns West of 'all weapons' use if Russia’s exclave Kaliningrad is attacked
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday warned the West against escalating the war in Ukraine, saying Russia could use “all weapons” in its arsenal,
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday warned the West against escalating the war in Ukraine, saying Russia could use “all weapons” in its arsenal, including nuclear weapons, if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad comes under attack.Speaking at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow, Putin said Russia had no plans to attack any European country but would respond if it faced what he described as Western aggression. He specifically pointed to Kaliningrad, a Russian territory located between Nato members Poland and Lithuania.“If it comes to direct attack against the Russian Federation, in this case on Kaliningrad and possibly some other territories, of course the issue of using all weapons in our country’s arsenal will inevitably and unavoidably emerge on the agenda. This is unavoidable,” Putin said.“The drills in the Baltic Sea, following one another … Then the attempts to arrest our ships and vessels. All this is an escalation. And then we began to hear statements regarding the Kaliningrad region,” Putin said.Putin says Ukraine strikes hitting Russian economyPutin also acknowledged that Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries were hurting the country’s economy, saying they had cost Russia about 1% of its GDP, CNN reported.Ukraine has stepped up long-range drone attacks on Russian territory, particularly targeting oil infrastructure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has described the strikes as “long-range sanctions” intended to cut Russia’s revenues and military capacity and push Moscow towards negotiations.Putin said Ukrainian attacks had also damaged more than 100 Russian ships in the Black Sea.Why is Kaliningrad strategically important?Kaliningrad is a strategically important Russian territory surrounded by Nato members Poland and Lithuania. It is a heavily militarised Russian exclave, meaning it is separated from Russia’s main territory. Located between Poland and Lithuania on the Baltic Sea, the region has a population of about 1 million and covers an area slightly larger than the US state of Connecticut, Reuters reports.The exclave gives Russia a key military position in the Baltic region, hosting air defence, missile and naval capabilities that can project power into parts of northern and central Europe.But its location also makes it vulnerable. Surrounded by Nato territory on its landward sides and separated from mainland Russia, maintaining supply lines or reinforcing the region could become difficult during a conflict.Tensions around Kaliningrad have grown since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, as Nato strengthened its eastern flank.You use AI every day. articles.body: Team USA returned from the 2026 International Artificial Intelligence Olympiad (IAIO) in Ljubljana, Slovenia, with four students earning four distinctions. Peter Xiao, a senior at Montgomery High School in Silver Spring, Maryland, earned the silver medal, while Aaditya Bilakanti and Jerry Yu received honourable mentions. Together, the students earned one gold medal, one silver medal, and two honourable mentions.Team members were selected through the 2025 USA-North America AI OlympiadThe four students reached the international competition through the 2025 USA-North America AI Olympiad. articles.title: Gulf oil infrastructure at risk as US rushes Patriot missiles to Saudi Arabia, Qatar amid Iran tensions
articles.summary: The US military has deployed two additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar, strengthening protection around key oil and gas
articles.body: The US military has deployed two additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar, strengthening protection around key oil and gas facilities as Washington prepares for the possibility of renewed major military operations against Iran.According to Axios, citing two US officials and one regional source, the deployments come after Saudi and Qatari leaders raised concerns that Iran could retaliate against their energy infrastructure if the US resumes large scale attacks on Tehran.One Patriot battery was sent to Saudi Arabia to protect a key oil facility, while another was deployed to Qatar to protect a natural gas facility, Axios reported.The move highlights the risk to Gulf energy infrastructure if the US Iran conflict escalates again.In early August, when US President Donald Trump was considering a major attack that included strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, the leaders of Saudi Arabia and Qatar reportedly lobbied him against the plan, fearing Iranian retaliation against their oil and natural gas facilities, according to Axios.Any major attack on oil or gas infrastructure in the region could disrupt energy supplies and put further pressure on global markets, particularly if the conflict affects shipping through key regional waterways.The additional Patriot deployments also come as the US faces growing pressure on its missile defence stocks. Patriot batteries, and particularly their interceptors, have become increasingly sought after since the Iran war began.According to the analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that US Patriot interceptor inventories had fallen below 1,000 following extensive use during the Iran conflict.The Pentagon is meanwhile expanding its military presence in the Middle East, with additional warships, fighter aircraft and troops being sent to the region.The Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, carrying thousands of US Marines, has also been deployed to the region, adding to Washington’s growing military presence in the Middle East.About Patriot air defence systemThe Patriot air and missile defence system is a ground based system operated by the US and allied militaries to protect troops and critical infrastructure from aerial threats.The US Army says Patriot can defend against aircraft, cruise missiles and tactical ballistic missiles, with its fire unit built around a radar, engagement control station and launchers.The latest PAC 3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) interceptor uses hit to kill technology, destroying incoming threats through direct impact. It is powered by a two pulse solid rocket motor that gives it greater range, altitude and manoeuvrability than earlier PAC 3 versions.A Patriot fire unit typically includes a multifunction radar, engagement control station and launchers. Depending on configuration, a launcher can carry up to 12 PAC 3 MSE interceptors.

articles.title: OpenAI fires 3 researchers as AI safety concerns intensify across the tech industry
articles.summary: OpenAI has fired three researchers after an internal investigation found they had allegedly mishandled sensitive information and breached company rules.
articles.body: OpenAI has fired three researchers after an internal investigation found they had allegedly mishandled sensitive information and breached company rules.The San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company did not publicly identify the researchers, but the Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg reported that they were Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni. At least two of them worked on AI safety and alignment, areas focused on making advanced AI systems behave safely and follow human instructions."We have parted ways with three individuals," OpenAI told news agency AFP in a statement."Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work."The company did not provide details about what information was allegedly mishandled. The Wall Street Journal reported that the matter involved work connected to an external organisation that evaluates AI models. The researchers did not immediately respond to AFP's requests for comment.Firings come amid growing AI safety debateThe dismissals come at a time when researchers inside major AI companies are increasingly raising concerns about the risks of developing increasingly powerful systems.Last month, 27-year-old researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic and warned that leading AI companies, including OpenAI, where he had previously worked, were "gambling with our lives" by competing to develop more powerful AI models.The three researchers named in reports about the OpenAI firings had also been publicly discussing AI safety concerns.Balesni wrote on September 10, "i am at OpenAI and i think AI is >10% likely to kill all humans," echoing concerns expressed by other AI researchers.Korbak also criticised aspects of OpenAI's approach on September 11, writing, "I'm quite unhappy with much of what OpenAI does. I am very happy that Im allowed to say 'I’m quite unhappy with much of what OpenAI does.'"Wang, responding to Coxon's resignation, wrote, "It's hard to overstate how dangerous speeding towards RSI is," referring to recursive self-improvement. This describes systems that are designed to improve their own capabilities continuously.Tech giants promise stronger safeguardsThe debate over AI safety has also reached the White House. Major US technology companies agreed this week to a voluntary safety pledge following a meeting with President Donald Trump. The companies involved included Nvidia, Google, Meta, xAI, OpenAI and Anthropic.Trump described the agreement as a "morally binding" commitment to ensure that adequate safeguards are developed as AI technology advances.The pledge comes as concerns grow over whether increasingly autonomous AI systems can be controlled and whether companies are moving too quickly in the race to build more capable models. OpenAI has faced several safety and security concerns in recent months.The company cancelled the release of a model called Astra 6.1 after determining that it was unreliable and frequently failed to follow instructions. It instead launched GPT-6.1 Sol, an updated version of another model, at its annual DevDay conference in San Francisco on Tuesday. OpenAI said Sol would cost one-fifth as much as Astra.In July, AI agents developed by OpenAI were involved in an incident in which the autonomous systems attacked Hugging Face, an AI model and application library, after escaping their controlled testing environment.Other security incidents involving AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google have since been reported.Cybersecurity firm Asymmetric Security said on Thursday that it had found another concerning case involving OpenAI systems. According to the firm, AI agents had gained unauthorised access to government websites and then attempted to conceal what they had done.The Washington Post also reported on Wednesday that the Federal Trade Commission had opened a broad investigation into AI safety practices at Anthropic and OpenAI. The exact scope of that investigation remains unclear.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Ford CEO Jim Farley makes clear distinction of the jobs that AI cannot replace; says automation cannot be done for ...
articles.summary: Ford CEO Jim Farley has made a clear distinction between the types of jobs artificial intelligence is likely to replace and the ones that will remain
articles.body: Ford CEO Jim Farley has made a clear distinction between the types of jobs artificial intelligence is likely to replace and the ones that will remain dependent on human expertise, arguing that skilled trades workers will largely be protected from the first wave of AI disruption. According to a report by Fortune, speaking during a backstage media roundtable at Ford Pro Accelerate, Farley emphasised that AI would increasingly function as a ‘companion’ for workers in factories, repair shows and skilled-trades occupations instead of a replacement. “I think most of these jobs will be both using AI and also protected from it,” Farley said. However, he warned that more routine white-collar roles face greater disruption. “If you work in finance doing spreadsheets, or you're in a call centre, or you're an entry-level programmer, those jobs are definitely going to be changed and eliminated with at least this first inning of AI.”AI cannot automate practical judgement, says Ford CEOFarley argued that AI is likely to struggle to replace workers whose jobs require hands-on problem-solving, physical expertise and real-world judgement. Electricians, technicians, mechanics and factory skilled-trades workers will continue to be needed even as automation becomes more advanced, he said.According to Farley, these roles will increasingly involve working alongside AI-powered systems, robots and automation tools, but humans will still be responsible for diagnosing failures, applying practical knowledge and ensuring work is completed safely.At Ford, the shift is already underway. The automaker employs more than 10,000 skilled-trades workers, representing roughly 20% of its 56,000 UAW-represented workforce. Many of these workers now spend less time maintaining traditional mechanical equipment and more time working with robots, automated production systems and digital manufacturing technologies.Line between engineer and technician is blurringFarley said technological advances are making it increasingly difficult to distinguish between engineering roles and skilled trades positions inside modern factories.“The visible line now, it's kind of hard to tell when an engineer or a manufacturing engineer stops, and the skilled trade starts in these newer type operations,” he said.In newer Ford plants, skilled-trades employees may maintain robotic casting systems, troubleshoot battery manufacturing equipment or configure digital production processes. Some tasks, Farley noted, increasingly resemble work performed in semiconductor manufacturing facilities rather than traditional automotive factories.Already happening inside FordFarley said this shift is already visible on Ford's own factory floors. The company currently employs more than 10,000 skilled-trades workers, representing roughly 20% of its 56,000 UAW workforce. Increasingly, that work is moving beyond traditional maintenance of conveyors and mechanical systems toward repairing robots, handling fiber optic systems, maintaining automated equipment, and operating within increasingly digitized manufacturing environments.He noted that the boundary between skilled trades and engineering has become genuinely blurry inside Ford's newer manufacturing operations, where skilled-trades workers now maintain large robotic casting systems, configure digital manufacturing processes, and troubleshoot equipment used in battery production — work Farley compared more closely to semiconductor fabrication than to a traditional auto plant.Trust remains critical for AI adoptionDespite the productivity benefits, Farley acknowledged that workers may be sceptical if they believe AI tools are being used for surveillance or could threaten their jobs.Ford already uses AI-powered vision systems to help inspect vehicle components and improve manufacturing quality. However, Farley stressed that companies must ensure workers trust how data generated by those systems is used.“If they don't trust that the data's going to be used the right way, somehow against them or somehow in a not-so-nice way, it's going to be a problem,” he said.An old tension in a new formFarley framed the current anxiety around AI in manufacturing as a modern version of a much older dynamic: the historical skepticism workers have shown toward time-and-motion studies, an industrial management practice built around timing workers' tasks to identify efficiency improvements. He recalled a personal experience early in his career conducting time-and-motion studies, when a worker several years older than him confronted him during a break after noticing he was being timed, directly accusing him of trying to take his job.Farley said he doesn't see today's AI-driven efficiency tools as fundamentally different from that earlier tension between management's view of a system as an efficiency tool and workers' instinct to see it as surveillance or a threat to their livelihood — suggesting that managing trust, not just deploying the technology itself, will determine how smoothly AI integrates into skilled-trades work going forward.You use AI every day. articles.title: India needs different financing model for Commercial EVs than it used for cars
articles.summary: This article is authored by Mahesh Babu, Managing Director, Olectra Greentech Ltd. India is entering a new phase in the way it moves people and goods.
articles.body: This article is authored by Mahesh Babu, Managing Director, Olectra Greentech Ltd.India is entering a new phase in the way it moves people and goods. The scale of this transformation is immense: the country transports approximately 4.6 billion tonnes of freight every year, with road transport carrying around 70% of domestic freight demand, measured in tonne-kilometres. And this demand is only set to grow. The road freight activity could reach approximately 9.6 trillion tonne-kilometres by 2050. While, on the other hand, 40 crores of passengers move everyday in the buses.This growth presents India with a remarkable opportunity; not just to move more, but to move smarter and more sustainably. The vehicles at the heart of India’s economy are also among the most intensively used on its roads. Trucks and buses move millions of people and tonnes of goods every day, while together accounting for around 60% of India’s diesel consumption.That makes the electrification of trucks and buses one of the most significant opportunities in India’s transition to cleaner mobility. The opportunity goes far beyond replacing diesel with electricity. Electrifying these high-utilisation vehicles can help reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, lower transport emissions, improve operating economics and strengthen India’s energy security.India has the chance to turn the scale of its freight and public transport networks into an advantage building a cleaner, more efficient and more resilient mobility system for the decades ahead.Policy is already creating the foundation for this transition. Under PM E DRIVE,₹4,391 crore has been allocated for 14,028 electric buses, ₹500 crore for 5,643 electric trucks and ₹2,000 crore for public charging infrastructure. The PM e Bus Sewa Payment Security Mechanism has a further outlay of ₹3,435 crore and aims to support more than 38,000 electric buses.The opportunity is substantial. Converting it into adoption at scale will require technology, charging infrastructure and financing to progress together.Three important Pillars to power the EV Revolution in IndiaThe next phase of electric vehicle adoption will depend on three key pillars:Technology, Charging infrastructure and Financing.Vehicle technology is advancing rapidly. Improvements in battery performance, driving range, energy efficiency and connected-vehicle capabilities are makingEVs increasingly practical for a wider range of consumers. At the same time, charging infrastructure is expanding, supported by growing public and private investment.The third pillar-financing becomes the third and very important enabler. The right financing models, competitive lending products and easier access to credit can help make electric passenger vehicles more affordable and accessible to consumers. As the technology and charging ecosystem mature, ensuring that customers can finance EVs as easily as conventional vehicles will be critical to accelerating adoption.An electric commercial vehicle is a productive asset that generates revenue every day over several years. Its financing structure should therefore reflect its earning potential and productive life.This is particularly important because the acquisition cost of an electric truck or bus can currently be around 2.5 times that of a comparable with fossil fuel commercial vehicles. Financing can also carry an interest premium of 2% to 4%, together with shorter tenures.When a higher asset cost is amortised over a conventional four- or five-year financing period, monthly repayments can become challenging even when the vehicle offers attractive economics over its full operating life.A financing horizon of around six to seven years, depending on the application and asset, can better align repayment with the productive life of the vehicle and the operator’s cash flows.Financial Innovation Must Now Move Alongside Technology Innovation.Financing should follow the earning life of the asset. Commercial EV financing can increasingly be based on the productive value of the vehicle.Daily kilometres, assured utilisation, energy cost, uptime, maintenance requirements and operating revenue provide a strong picture of the economics of a commercial asset.An electric bus operating under a long-term contract with assured kilometres offers visibility of utilisation and cash flows. Similarly, an electric truck operating on a defined logistics corridor can build a predictable operating profile.Financing structures that recognise these cash flows can make EV adoption more accessible.This becomes particularly important in India, where around 70% of truck operators have fleets of five vehicles or fewer. For these operators, predictable monthly cash flow is critical.The financing model therefore needs to align with both the productive life of the vehicle and the economics of the operator.Leasing can widen accessLong term leasing can become another important enabler.Instead of carrying the entire acquisition cost upfront, operators can access vehicles through models that convert a larger part of the investment into predictable operating expenditure.Vehicle leasing and Battery as a Service can also distribute technology and residual value risks among participants better equipped to manage them. These both models are potential pathways for accelerating electric truck adoption, particularly among smaller operators.This can make commercial EVs more accessible while allowing operators to focus on keeping vehicles productive and generating revenue.Connected vehicles can make financing smarterTechnology can also strengthen one of the most important elements of vehicle financing: residual value.Electric commercial vehicles are increasingly connected assets. Battery State of Health, charging cycles, kilometres travelled, energy efficiency, uptime and maintenance history can be continuously measured.This data can create a transparent digital health record for the vehicle, giving lenders greater visibility into asset performance throughout its operating life.The same digital technology transforming the vehicle can also transform the way the vehicle is financed.A robust battery health and vehicle performance framework can strengthen residual value assessment, support the secondary market and improve lender confidence.Financial innovation can accelerate adoptionIndia can build commercial electric mobility at scale. Technology will continue to advance, charging infrastructure will expand and policy support is creating the foundation for growth.Financing can become the multiplier.Longer tenure loans, long term leasing, cash flow-based financing, connected vehicle data and stronger residual value frameworks can make electric buses and trucks increasingly bankable and accessible.When financing is aligned with the productive life and earning potential of the asset, commercial EVs become a stronger business proposition for operators and financiers alike.Technology will enable the transition. Infrastructure will support it. Financial innovation can accelerate commercial EV adoption at scale.Disclaimer: Views and opinions expressed in this article are solely those of the original author and do not represent any of The Times Group or its employees.

articles.title: ‘Bindass Mumbai boy, go-to guy at flying school’: Friends recall Smit Machchhar as calm, cheerful pilot before he saved 174
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Long before Captain Smit Machchhar became the pilot who fought through serious injuries to help save 174 people aboard a flydubai flight, friends
articles.body: MUMBAI: Long before Captain Smit Machchhar became the pilot who fought through serious injuries to help save 174 people aboard a flydubai flight, friends and neighbours knew him as a calm, cheerful and down-to-earth man who was always willing to help.“Smit is the most calm, composed and down-to-earth person you could ever meet,” said Capt Dharav Gosalia, a friend who has known Machchhar since their flying school days.On Wednesday, that composure was tested at altitude when flydubai flight FZ1073, carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, came under attack inside the cockpit. According to Israeli officials, Machchhar’s co-pilot stabbed him and attempted to crash the aircraft. The plane reportedly plunged nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds.Seriously injured, Machchhar managed to regain control of the aircraft and open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker. The flight eventually made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. Machchhar, 39, is recovering in Abu Dhabi.Those who knew him said his response in the crisis reflected the personality they had seen for years.“He is one of the calmest and most fun guys possible,” said a friend, a B737 pilot who requested anonymity. “Maybe it is his upbringing. He is always in fun mode, but he is family-oriented too.”‘Everyone went to him when they had a problem’Machchhar earned his commercial pilot licence from Mainland Aviation College in New Zealand in the late 2000s. His classmates soon came to rely on him whenever they struggled with their studies.“Anyone with a problem in air navigation, aircraft technical or any subject went to him,” the pilot said.His career later took him to flydubai, where he became a Boeing 737 captain and line trainer.His willingness to help was not limited to colleagues. Friends said Machchhar treated loaders, engineers, ground staff and catering workers with the same respect he showed fellow pilots.At M D Bhatia School, where he completed Class 10 in 2003, school friend Bhavin Jethva remembered him as “straightforward, bindass”.“He didn’t like to lie. He was never fake and he couldn’t pretend,” Jethva said.Another childhood friend, Amit Soni, who played cricket with Machchhar, recalled him as cheerful and lively.Former classmates have since been posting prayers for his recovery on their WhatsApp group. “We are proud of him,” Jethva said.From Tilak Nagar to the cockpitMachchhar lived at Swastik Heights in Mumbai’s Tilak Nagar until around 2022. Neighbour Laxmikanth Joshi recalled several small gestures that reflected his helpful nature.After returning from Kenya, Joshi realised he had bought too little coffee to share with friends. Machchhar arranged for a pilot colleague to bring more.Joshi also remembered Machchhar rushing to a hospital after returning to India when his father underwent bypass surgery about six months ago. He stayed with him through the treatment.During Independence Day and Republic Day celebrations in the society, Machchhar also helped residents with the flag-hoisting arrangements. Joshi recalled that he taught them how to tie the rope properly so that “one pull and the flag unfurled”.Machchhar moved to Dubai around 2022 after leaving SpiceJet. He and his wife, Sonal, have two children, Krishay, 2, and Ziva, 9.His parents informed residents of their society through a WhatsApp group late Wednesday that he was recovering after the attack.As tributes poured in from across the world, US President Donald Trump called Machchhar a “hero”. Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised his courage and presence of mind, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the captain’s actions helped prevent a catastrophic mid-air disaster.For those who knew him before the headlines, however, Machchhar remains the same person they remember — the calm pilot, the cheerful friend and the “bindass” Mumbai boy who was always ready to help.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: How India's classrooms are coping in the age  of instant gratification & low attention spans?
articles.summary: Classrooms in parts of India are quietly grappling with an underlying problem that no curriculum revision can easily fix.
articles.body: Classrooms in parts of India are quietly grappling with an underlying problem that no curriculum revision can easily fix. Students raised on on-demand food delivery, constant social media reels and instant AI answers are finding it harder to sustain attention, tolerate boredom, or work toward rewards that don't arrive at once.Teachers, as a result, are increasingly engaging a generation that is much less attentive than before. A recent nationwide survey by the National Council of CBSE Schools found that almost 70% of teachers across the country have observed a sharp decline in their students' focus and classroom attention.The survey, which covered around 6.3 lakh respondents -- teachers, under 18 students and their parents -- also found that 74% of students spend more than two hours a day on screen for non-academic purposes. And teachers reported rising anxiety, irritability and reduced face-to-face interaction among children.Parmeshwar Dattarao Bhurke, a teacher, says the trend is evident in everyday classroom experiences. "Many children no longer have the focus needed to sit through an hour-long lesson or read a passage without their minds wandering," he said. This has prompted many teachers to experiment with newer learning methods, he added. "Earlier, one student could read a chapter aloud while the rest of the class listened. That no longer works... The idea now is to keep their minds actively engaged through the session."Priya, another middle school teacher, says she has noticed a decline in students' retention levels. "Even when children appear to be listening, their minds are elsewhere. They are also less willing to struggle through any difficult task. This affects their performance in school as well as their behaviour, as they become averse to any kind of challenges or discomfort."For 15-year-old student Chinmayee Sonna, the shift is visible in the way her classmates now study. "Instead of sitting with textbooks or working through ideas, many of my classmates look for the easier option, whether that is AI-generated summaries or explainer videos. They are able to retain less through this method but it helps revise quickly and saves time," she said.Psychologists say such habits reflect a behavioural shift driven by constant access to instant rewards. "They trigger dopamine, giving us a brief rush of joy that reinforces the behaviour and makes us want to repeat it. This is different from the real-life feats, where satisfaction comes only after much effort and patience," Rashi Bhatnagar, a psychologist, said.It is these consequences that extend into the classroom. "When rewards come with almost no effort, the brain begins to prefer them. Like an unused muscle, our ability to wait, tolerate boredom and sustain attention gradually weakens, leaving us restless when tasks demand patience," Bhatnagar said.This is why there is a downside to schools trying to make every lesson entertaining, she adds. "Education cannot always provide instant pleasure if it is to encourage deep thinking. Schools need to consciously create opportunities for children to reflect and generate new ideas."The habit of expecting immediate outcomes also affects resilience. "Because children have not developed the ability to wait for results, many give up too quickly. We need to teach them not to quit at the first sign of difficulty," Bhatnagar said.Psychiatrist Nisha Singla, talking about the digital ecosystem, says it is deliberately designed to reinforce instant gratification. "Social media apps, notifications and quick commerce applications are addictive and the brain begins to crave them. Reading or learning something new also gives us a sense of achievement, but the reward is delayed. That is where all the difference lies."Rebuilding patience, she says, begins with allowing children to slow down. "We need to let them get bored... There is a tendency to fill every moment of their day with something or the other, but boredom is equally important. Parents and schools should consciously encourage delayed gratification."Another challenge to consider in adapting classrooms is large class sizes and poor teacher-student ratios. "This leaves little room for us to nurture each child's curiosity and individual learning needs. At the same time, schools remain under pressure to deliver high marks and pass percentages, leaving us focused on examination outcomes rather than redesigning learning around children's changing needs," Priya said.As educators wait for the national mental health and well-being policy for schools, they say it should help students find meaning in a learning process whose greatest rewards cannot be a sprint and a quick fix.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Shaadi.com founder and Shark Tank India judge Anupam Mittal has now shared his views on why many business plans fail.
articles.body: Shaadi.com founder and Shark Tank India judge Anupam Mittal has now shared his views on why many business plans fail. In a post shared on professional social networking platform LinkedIn, Mittal argued that companies often mistake activity for progress by focusing on long to-do lists instead of solving the few issues that really matter. Mittal said that businesses do not succeed by creating plans filled with dozens of tasks. “You don't win with a long list of things to do," he wrote.As per Mittal, many of the organisations create plans consisting of 25 to 50 items that need to be checked off, creating what he described as a "false sense of progress" as teams focus on completing tasks rather than addressing the main obstacles holding back growth. Mittal also believed that most companies are typically constrained by only one other two major bottlenecks at any given time. "In a company or team, usually 1 or 2 bottlenecks are holding everything back," Mittal said. He added that the role of leadership is to identify those critical constraints and direct resources toward solving them."The job of leadership is simple. Find those. articles.title: Taiwan to receive first new F-16 Viper jets from US: How are they different from older Falcons?
articles.summary: Taiwan is set to receive the first two of 66 newly built F-16V or Viper fighter jets under a US deal worth around $8 billion, as Taipei moves to
articles.body: Taiwan is set to receive the first two of 66 newly built F-16V or Viper fighter jets under a US deal worth around $8 billion, as Taipei moves to strengthen its air defences amid growing Chinese military activity around the island.According to Reuters, the first two aircraft are due to arrive at Taiwan's Taitung Air Base on Friday, marking the start of deliveries under the long-delayed programme.Taiwan Defence Minister Wellington Koo said more F-16Vs would arrive before the end of the year, with the deliveries eventually taking the island's F-16 fleet to more than 200 aircraft.The $8 billion deal was approved by the United States in 2019 and covers 66 new F-16V aircraft built by Lockheed Martin. The programme faced delays linked to production and software issues, with deliveries originally expected to begin earlier.Taiwan has also upgraded its existing fleet of F-16A/B fighters to the F-16V standard under a separate modernisation programme. The upgrades have given the older aircraft newer avionics, radar and other systems, while the latest order involves brand-new F-16V Block 70 fighters.The delivery of the first F-16Vs comes just days after US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a summit in Washington, where Taiwan remained a key point of tension between the two countries.The arrival also comes amid uncertainty over Washington's future arms support for Taipei, despite repeated assurances from US officials that there has been no change in policy toward Taiwan.Taiwan is still waiting for the Trump administration to approve a new arms package worth about $14 billion, which has remained on hold for months.Trump said in May, after meeting Xi in Beijing, that he was keeping the package “in abeyance”, while the US had approved a separate $11 billion arms package in December 2025.China has repeatedly opposed US arms sales to Taiwan and had urged Washington to exercise “extreme caution” over such deals ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.How the Viper is different from older FalconsTaiwan's new F-16V Block 70 fighters retain the basic design of the F-16 Fighting Falcon but come with a substantially modernised electronics and mission systems suite.The biggest upgrade is the AN/APG-83 AESA radar, which provides improved detection, tracking and targeting capabilities compared with the mechanically scanned radars fitted to many older F-16s.Lockheed Martin says the radar incorporates technology from the AESA systems developed for the F-22 and F-35.The Viper also gets a modernised mission computer, upgraded avionics, high-resolution cockpit display, high-speed data bus and advanced datalink capabilities.These systems allow pilots to process and share battlefield information more quickly and support modern precision-guided weapons and targeting systems.Another major difference is the Automatic Ground Collision Avoidance System (Auto GCAS), designed to automatically help prevent an aircraft from crashing into terrain if the pilot becomes unable to recover the aircraft.The new Block 70 also has a strengthened airframe designed for a 12,000-hour service life, more than 50 percent higher than previous production F-16s, according to Lockheed Martin.

articles.title: Windrush compensation funds British Caribbean playwright prize
articles.summary: The winning dramatist will receive £10,000, publication and a professional theatre production.
articles.body:
A theatre producer has used compensation awarded in her late father's Windrush case to launch a national prize dedicated to British Caribbean playwrights.

It is believed to be the first initiative of its kind in 30 years, and offers a £10,000 award, publication and a professional theatre production.

Actor and former criminal barrister Shereener Browne set up the prize to discover and nurture British Caribbean playwrights and address their underrepresentation on UK stages.

She said: "It was borne out of a great injustice suffered by my late father and others from the Caribbean, so I honour his memory by creating a prize to elevate our stories, create opportunities and effect lasting change."

Browne's father, Myron Brown, lived and worked in Britain for decades and was effectively made stateless by the government when he was refused documentation required to prove his status as a British citizen.

Although he was successful in his claim from the Windrush Compensation Scheme, the settlement was awarded after his death.

Browne said the Windrush Prize "was deeply personal" to her.

She added: "Black History Month is about recognising the people, stories and experiences that have shaped Black Britain and the Windrush Prize is about ensuring those stories continue to be told by a new generation."

The Windrush Prize for British Caribbean Playwrights is open to UK-based British Caribbean writers over 18 years of age.

Submissions must be unpublished, full-length plays and both represented and unrepresented writers are eligible to apply.

The prize includes mentorship, development opportunities, public readings, and production support alongside the main award.

Entrants can apply between 2 October and 2 December.

articles.title: Devon A-level student starts her own fashion line
articles.summary: Gracie, 16, says she got the idea to start her own brand while modelling at London Fashion Week.
articles.body:
A teenage model has launched her own fashion label while still studying for her A-levels.

Gracie, 16, from Tavistock said she got the idea of setting up her own clothing company while modelling on the catwalk at London Fashion Week.

Back home in her bedroom, she got to work designing a hoodie which she believes have a unique selling point.

The teenage designer said the hoodies were a single colour on the outside but have a polka dot material lining the hood.

Gracie said she was 14 when she was spotted by a talent scout at a Taylor Swift concert. By the age of 15 she was on the catwalk at London Fashion Week.

While there she thought that while it was "really cool wearing other people's clothes" it would be better if she could create something other people wanted to wear.

Once she had the idea for her hoodies she moved quickly to get them into production under her brand Bloom House.

"I had the sketches, picked out some colours, found a factory and now we're making them," she said.

Gracie said her parents, Mitch and Lei, inspired her as both run their own businesses.

Mitch said his daughter sought different quotes and fabrics and tested everything "all off her own bat".

"She's keen and she wants to do this but we'll be here in the background," he said.

Lei said even if Gracie's new company did not "go global" it would always be "a really good start."

As well as running her own business and modelling, Gracie has a part-time job in a restaurant, runs her own social media platforms and is studying business, economics, psychology and core maths for her A-levels.

"I've always been pretty good with time management, so if I keep that hopefully it shouldn't get too much," she said.

articles.title: Jamie Oliver saves Essex airfield that trained him
articles.summary: After qualifying as a pilot, the TV chef helps arrange new ownership for an Essex aviation company.
articles.body:
Jamie Oliver has stepped in to save the airfield and flying school where he trained to be a pilot.

The owners at Andrewsfield Aviation, near Braintree in Essex, said they were preparing to close operations because there was no successor lined up after they retired.

But the TV chef, who achieved his pilot licence in July, helped arrange new ownership to ensure the hangar doors remained open.

"Andrewsfield is a special place with so much potential," said Oliver, who is from Essex.

"It has an extraordinary history and is full of wonderful people with an exemplary training environment that has changed my life for the better."

Carol Cooper and Michael Rowland, the directors of Andrewsfield Aviation Ltd, had said that without a "suitable succession plan, the only realistic option may have been to close" the company.

The airfield was used by the RAF and United States Air Force during World War Two.

But Oliver helped arrange new ownership by bringing in Marc Naylor, also known as Blondie, as the major shareholder and day-to-day operator.

Oliver praised Naylor's "infectious energy and aviation experience", having spent a decade with the air ambulance in Devon.

Naylor said Andrewsfield already had a "special place in my heart", describing it as a "community built on friendships, shared memories and a passion for aviation".

Cooper will continue as a flying instructor and examiner at the airfield.

With more than 27,000 hours of flying under her belt, her new target is 30,000.

Oliver grew up in Clavering near Saffron Walden and moved close to Finchingfield village more recently.

He continued: "I will remain closely involved as a supporter [of the airfield] and will help wherever I can."
